1.title: Lesson 1: What is Cryptocurrency?
1.description: Cryptocurrency is digital money that works without banks. Bitcoin was created in 2009 and is the first and most well-known cryptocurrency. Unlike traditional currencies, Bitcoin is not controlled by any central bank — it's governed by a network of computers worldwide. Think of it as digital gold: only 21 million Bitcoin will ever exist, and no more can be created. Other popular cryptocurrencies include Ethereum (a platform for smart contracts), Solana (known for fast transactions), and thousands of others.

2.title: Lesson 2: Blockchain — The Technology Behind It
2.description: Blockchain is the technology that makes Bitcoin possible. Imagine a digital notebook copied to thousands of computers simultaneously. Every time someone sends Bitcoin, the transaction is written in the notebook. All copies update at the same time, and no one can change old entries. This is called 'decentralized' because no single person controls the book. The word 'blockchain' literally means a 'chain of blocks'. Every 10 minutes, new transactions are collected into a block, and this block is linked to the previous one. The result is an unbreakable chain showing the entire history of all Bitcoin transactions ever made.

3.title: Lesson 3: Crypto Wallet — Your Digital Safe
3.description: To own crypto, you need a crypto wallet. There are two main types: 'hot wallets' (apps on your phone that are easy to use, e.g., Metamask or Trust Wallet) and 'cold wallets' (physical devices like Ledger or Trezor that keep your crypto offline and extra safe). The wallet contains two keys: a public key (like an account number you can share with others to receive crypto) and a private key (like your PIN — it MUST be kept secret). If you lose the private key, you lose access to your crypto permanently. Therefore, it is critical to make backups.

4.title: Lesson 4: How to Buy Bitcoin
4.description: The easiest way is to use a regulated exchange like Coinbase or Binance. Create an account, verify your identity, and transfer money via bank transfer. You do NOT need to buy a whole Bitcoin! You can buy a small fraction — for example $50 worth. When you trade, you pay a small fee (usually 0.1%-1.5%). After buying, you can leave the crypto on the exchange (convenient but some risk) or move it to your own wallet (safer). Tip: Start with a small amount you can afford to lose, and get comfortable with the process before increasing.

5.title: Lesson 5: Security — Protect Your Crypto
5.description: The crypto world has scammers, and you must protect yourself. The most important rules: (1) NEVER share your private key/seed phrase with anyone — no legitimate service will ask for it. (2) Always use 2-factor authentication (2FA) with an app like Google Authenticator, not SMS. (3) Beware of phishing — scammers create fake websites that look like Binance/Coinbase. Always check the URL. (4) Use strong, unique passwords for crypto accounts. (5) Consider a hardware wallet for larger amounts. (6) Don't share how much crypto you own on social media. Finally: no legitimate person promises 'guaranteed returns' in crypto.

1.title: Lesson 1: Technical Analysis
1.description: Technical analysis is about studying price history and charts to predict future movements. By looking at patterns, volume, and various indicators, traders try to identify 'trends' (direction) and 'support/resistance' (price levels where the market often turns). Unlike fundamental analysis, which looks at the value of a project, technical analysis focuses solely on price action. It is a powerful tool, but it's important to remember that it's not a crystal ball — it only gives you probabilities, not certainties.

quiz.question: What does a 'golden cross' indicate?
quiz.funFact: A golden cross occurs when the 50-day moving average crosses above the 200-day moving average.

1.title: Lesson 1: What is DeFi?
1.description: Decentralized Finance (DeFi) is an ecosystem of financial applications built on blockchain technology (mainly Ethereum). Unlike traditional finance, DeFi works without intermediaries like banks or brokers. Instead, it uses 'smart contracts' to automate transactions. This allows you to lend, borrow, and trade assets 24/7 from anywhere in the world. It provides better transparency, lower fees, and access for everyone with an internet connection. Popular DeFi applications include Uniswap (trading), Aave (lending), and MakerDAO (decentralized stablecoins).

quiz.question: What is a smart contract?
quiz.funFact: Smart contracts were first proposed by Nick Szabo in 1994, long before Ethereum existed!
